proof.text: Use Noetherian local connectedness and the finite discrete space of connected components to partition Spec A into finitely many connected clopen opens. A clopen immersion is a closed immersion, hence affine, so all pieces are affine. This construction also gives the empty family on the empty scheme.

On each connected component, the values of the finite locally constant module sheaf are finite. Its underlying finite set sheaf is trivialized by a connected finite monodromy torsor. Upgrade this set trivialization to a constant module trivialization.

Choose an ell-Sylow subgroup H of the finite torsor group. The connected subgroup quotient supplies a connected H-torsor over a finite etale surjective cover V of the component, with every geometric fibre of size [P:H], which is positive and prime to ell. Its total space identifies with the original torsor. The pulled-back module sheaf is thus trivialized by this connected H-torsor.

The concrete finite-ring associated module functor recovers this pulled-back sheaf from an H-representation M. The natural torsor pullback comparison identifies every geometric stalk of T with its underlying module. A conservative family of geometric points therefore reflects finite limits and colimits, so T is exact. The unit comparison, finite presentations of finite modules, and finite products and cokernels show every finite trivial representation maps to a constant finite module sheaf. The same stalk comparison transfers finiteness and ell^n-annihilation to M.

Apply the proved primary finite p-group filtration to the additive representation of M. Take R-linear spans; stability and triviality of each successive action survive because the action is R-linear. Send the submodules through T. Exactness gives a monotone chain of actual Subobjects, with zero bottom, top endpoint, and cokernels equal to T of the quotient representations. The quotients are finite trivial H-modules, hence the preceding step supplies their constant-sheaf isomorphisms.

Let d be the product of the finitely many component degrees d_i, and repeat the i-th cover product_{j≠i} d_j times. Their finite coproduct is a finite etale surjective cover of Spec A; an explicit coproduct-fibre bijection proves every geometric fibre has size d. Product positivity and primality prove d≥1 and ell∤d. The summands form an affine clopen partition. Pull back each filtration along its summand isomorphism and use inverse-image composition to identify its sheaf with the desired restriction. The empty-base case is handled by the empty coproduct with d=1.

title: Prime-to-primary finite etale filtration cover for finite local systems
statement: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine with $A$ a Noetherian commutative ring [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], etale locally constant with finite module fibres [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Suppose $\ell$ is prime, $n\geq1$, and $\ell^n F=0$. There is a finite etale surjective morphism $g:T\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and an integer $d\geq1$ prime to $\ell$ such that every geometric fibre of $g$ has $d$ points [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]. Write $g^{-1}F$ for module inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Moreover, $T$ is a finite disjoint union of affine open-and-closed subschemes $T_a$, and for each $a$ the restriction of $g^{-1}F$ to $T_a$ has a finite filtration $0=F_{a,0}\subseteq F_{a,1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_{a,r_a}=g^{-1}F|_{T_a}$ by $\Lambda$-submodule sheaves whose successive quotients $F_{a,i+1}/F_{a,i}$ are constant sheaves of finite $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Empty schemes and zero sheaves are allowed.
